reuse.why: Adds a new getRangedAmount helper and routes getScheduledAmount through it, but the four server/preview sites keep their own missing/number/range dispatch instead of calling the existing getScheduledAmount, which already decides all three cases.

duplication.why: The range rule itself is now defined once, but the `== null ? 0 : number ? v : range` ternary stays copied across app.ts (twice), forecast-schedules.ts and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, duplicating getScheduledAmount.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getScheduledAmount, where the tree keeps schedule amount logic.

scope.why: Only the midpoint sites, a focused test and a release note are touched.

maintainability.why: A single named rule is easy to change again, though a maintainer still has to keep five parallel dispatch ternaries in sync.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedule-template.ts createScheduleList, forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule, schedules/app.ts updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule, shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions call getRangedAmount inside their own dispatch rather than getScheduledAmount

disguised_duplication.where: The remaining duplicated dispatch ternaries are pre-existing and left visibly as they were; the diff does not reshape them.

one_place.where: getRangedAmount in shared/schedules.ts; every ranged-amount path (getScheduledAmount, schedule templates, forecast, updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, preview) now calls it.
